title: Efficient split-state non-malleable codes approaching capacity
formal: Do uniform polynomial-time two-share nonmalleable codes exist with k message bits, equal share length ell(k), negligible statistical error in k, and rate k/(2 ell(k)) tending to 1/2 as k tends to infinity, against all independent tampering functions on the two shares?
definitions:
For each positive integer k, Enc_k is a randomized algorithm mapping {0,1}^k to pairs (L,R) in {0,1}^{ell(k)} squared. Dec_k is deterministic on every such pair and returns a k-bit message or a failure symbol bottom. The length ell(k) is computable in polynomial time and polynomially bounded. Both algorithms are uniform and run in polynomial time in k on every input and random tape; honest decoding equals the message with probability one. No shared setup secret or computational hardness is assumed.

For every pair of arbitrary deterministic maps f,g:{0,1}^{ell(k)} to {0,1}^{ell(k)}, there must exist a probability distribution D_{f,g} on {0,1}^k union {bottom,same} independent of the encoded message. For every message m, the total variation distance between Dec_k(f(L),g(R)), where (L,R) is sampled by Enc_k(m), and the following simulated variable is at most eta(k): sample d from D_{f,g}, output m if d=same, and otherwise output d. One and the same D_{f,g} must work for all m. The error eta is bounded by one negligible function uniformly over all f,g,m: for every c>0, eta(k)<k^{-c} eventually. The simulator need not be efficient.

Tampering maps may be computationally unbounded and know the public code but are fixed independently of the message and encoding randomness. Each sees only its own share; correlated choices of maps are covered by mixtures of deterministic pairs. The target is single-shot nonmalleability, not adaptive repeated tampering or leakage resilience. Rate counts both shares, and convergence to 1/2 is a single uniform family with ell(k)=k+o(k), not a claim about an unbounded-time existential code.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked uniform code family with perfect correctness, the statistical simulation property and the limiting rate, or prove that no such efficient family exists. Computational nonmalleability, bitwise tampering or more than two shares does not answer this information-theoretic two-share question.
context:
Two-share nonmalleability allows the original message to survive, but rules out a reliably related modified message after independent tampering.

Rate-one-third constructions approach the information-theoretic half-rate boundary but do not attain the limiting rate asked here.
why: This asks whether efficient split-state coding can reach its information-theoretic capacity.

import_provenance.original_title: Efficient split-state non-malleable codes approaching capacity
import_provenance.original_statement: Construct explicit, polynomial-time encodable and decodable, information-theoretic non-malleable codes against arbitrary independent tampering of two shares, with negligible error and rate approaching 1/2. This strengthens the split-state constructions developed by Aggarwal, Dodis and Lovett toward the information-theoretic capacity.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial continuation of Dodis’s constructions; the later rate-1/3 result does not attain capacity. Computational-security or additional-state constructions do not settle this information-theoretic two-share target.

sentences: An encoding splits a message into two equally long shares.
Each share may be changed by an arbitrary function unaware of the other share.
The decoded result must be either the original message or statistically independent of it.
Encoding and decoding must be uniform polynomial-time algorithms with negligible error.
The rate must tend to one half when both shares count toward length.
